title: How do you prevent cross-site scripting (XSS)?
description: Contextual output encoding, safe rich-HTML handling, CSP headers, and what React/Razor do for you.

data.text: **Question:** How do you prevent cross-site scripting (XSS)?

XSS happens when untrusted data reaches the page as **executable markup or script**. Prevent it by encoding output by default in the right context (HTML body, attribute, JavaScript, URL), sanitizing — with an allow-list — the rare fields that legitimately contain HTML, and adding a Content-Security-Policy header as a second layer. Frameworks like Razor and React already encode by default; vulnerabilities appear when you opt out (`@Html.Raw`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`).

**The three flavors:**
- **Stored** — the payload is saved (comment, profile bio) and served to every viewer; the most damaging
- **Reflected** — the payload is echoed from the request (search box, error page) in the response
- **DOM-based** — the server never sees it; client-side code moves data from `location.hash` or the DOM into `innerHTML`

**Layered defenses:**
- **Encode on output, in context** — HTML-encoding for markup, JavaScript escaping inside `<script>`, attribute encoding inside attributes, URL encoding in links. Encoding "once on input" can't know the context
- **Razor encodes by default** — `@Model.Comment` renders `<script>`; `@Html.Raw` is the explicit opt-out and must never touch user data
- **React encodes by default** — `{comment}` is safe; `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is named that way for a reason
- **Sanitize rich HTML** with an allow-list library (e.g. the `HtmlSanitizer` NuGet package) for markdown/editor output; block-list filters get bypassed
- **Content-Security-Policy** — `script-src 'self'` blocks injected and inline scripts even if encoding is missed; start in `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` and watch reports
- **HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite cookies** so injected script can't read session tokens

data.title: Encoding by default, CSP as a backstop

data.text:
Interviewers want to assess:
- Knowing XSS is about *context*, not about "filtering bad tags"
- Familiarity with the framework's default encoding and its escape hatches
- Layered thinking: encoding + sanitization + CSP + cookie flags
- Awareness of DOM-based XSS, which server-side filters never see

items: Stripping `<script>` tags but allowing event handlers (onerror, onload) — block-lists always miss something
Encoding on input instead of on output — the same value appears in HTML, attributes, and URLs
Escaping in the controller and rendering with @Html.Raw anyway
Assuming HTTPS or HttpOnly cookies prevent XSS — they limit damage, they don't stop execution
Ignoring DOM sinks: innerHTML, document.write, jQuery .html()
Deploying a hard CSP on day one without report-only — it silently breaks the app
What is the difference between stored, reflected, and DOM-based XSS?
How does a Content-Security-Policy actually block an injected payload?
How do you safely render user markdown (not raw HTML) on the client?
What is JSON hijacking and how does correct Content-Type relate to XSS?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: XSS = untrusted data executed as markup/script; encode per output context
Razor and React encode by default — @Html.Raw and dangerouslySetInnerHTML opt out
Sanitize legitimate rich HTML with an allow-list, never a block-list
CSP, HttpOnly and SameSite cookies are backstops, not replacements
data.takeaway: Encode by default, allow-list the exceptions, and let a CSP header catch whatever slips through — no single layer is enough.
